rationale: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה (oshb:Prov.20.5) and רָב אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא (oshb:Prov.20.6) run one shared construction: a bare man-noun, איש, stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both (word 5 of 8 in 20:5, word 5 of 9 in 20:6), and a waw-prefixed second instance of that noun, ואיש, answers it just past the caesura in both, opening the second colon in construct with an abstract quality noun — תבונה, "understanding," in 20:5 and אמונים, "faithfulness," in 20:6 — before both verses close on that second colon's own predicate, ידלנה in 20:5 and מי ימצא in 20:6. A word-bound sweep of this same-verse bare-plus-waw-prefixed doubling (whitespace-token equality against the consonantal skeleton) returns 2 of 915 verses book-wide, and both hits are the two verses of this span. The bare noun by itself, word-bound, is far more common (53 of 915 verses), and a contiguous-consonantal-substring sweep of the same bare form is wider still (87 of 915 verses); the paired, colon-symmetric doubling sets this pair apart from that wider background.
rejected_alternative: Treating 20:5 and 20:6 as two unrelated proverbs was rejected: the bare-plus-waw doubling that opens each verse's second colon is not the ordinary recurrence of a common noun but a paired, colon-symmetric construction, and a word-bound sweep of that exact doubling returns 2 of 915 verses book-wide, both of them this pair, so the two verses read as one deliberately constructed unit; extending the span to include Prov.20.4 or Prov.20.7 was also rejected, since neither neighboring verse shares a skeleton content token with either member of the pair.
observed_substrate_signals: same-verse bare-plus-waw doubling of the man-noun (word-bound, whitespace-token equality): 2 of 915 verses book-wide, both members of this pair
etnahta lands on word 5 in both verses (word 5 of 8 in Prov.20.5; word 5 of 9 in Prov.20.6)
the waw-prefixed second instance opens the second colon and stands in construct with an abstract quality noun in both verses
device_notes: The bare instance of the man-noun sits in a different slot in the two verses: it carries the etnahta itself in Prov.20.5, but stands one word ahead of the etnahta-bearing word in Prov.20.6. The two verses also run distinct images — deep water drawn out for hidden counsel in Prov.20.5, a claim of loyalty set against a rhetorical question about scarce faithfulness in Prov.20.6 — so the pairing runs a synthetic image in Prov.20.5 against a synthetic claim answered by an antithetic question in Prov.20.6, two different couplet textures joined by the shared bare-plus-waw construction.

rationale: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת (oshb:Prov.20.23) The line opens with the noun an abomination of Yahweh applied to differing weights, restating the same commerce concern from a different angle, and the closing clause about deceitful scales finishes the saying.
rejected_alternative: Reading this together with the steps-from-Yahweh saying that follows was set aside, since the commerce vocabulary here does not carry into the next verse's topic of a man's path; the divine name also closes the preceding verse (Prov.20.22) and opens the following one (Prov.20.24), but Yahweh is named too densely through the collection (an unprefixed token in 4 of chapter 20's 30 verses, 70 of 915 book-wide) to serve as a boundary driver on its own.
observed_substrate_signals: predicate noun abomination opens the restatement

rationale: חַבֻּר֣וֹת (oshb:Prov.20.30) The verse opens with the noun wound-stripes credited with cleansing evil; the noun naming that cleansing carries a ketiv/qere note (pmarks, single witness), and the parallel clause about blows reaching the inner chambers restates the same claim about painful correction, closing the chapter's saying as a paired restatement.
rejected_alternative: Reading this together with the king's-heart saying that opens the next chapter was dropped, because corrective punishment and providence over royal decisions share no wording.
observed_substrate_signals: inner-chamber clause restates and closes it

rationale: פַּלְגֵי (oshb:Prov.21.1) This couplet opens with the noun channels of water applied metaphorically to a king's heart in Yahweh's hand, and the relative clause about turning it wherever he desires completes the image within the verse.
rejected_alternative: Linking this verse to the one that follows was weighed because both name Yahweh and both carry the heart root — singular here, plural construct in the next verse — but the divine name is too dense through the collection (3 of chapter 21's verses, 70 of 915 book-wide) to serve as a driver, and the two heart terms sit in different syntactic slots with no shared clause template, so the watercourse image for the king's heart stands as its own unit and the pairing reads as thematic wisdom-lit texture rather than a deliberate catchword.

rationale: כָּֽל דֶּרֶךְ (oshb:Prov.21.2) The line opens with the phrase for a man's own way seeming right in his eyes, and the antithetic close in which Yahweh weighs the hearts supplies the corrective half that completes the couplet.
rejected_alternative: A merger with the saying just before it was weighed because both name Yahweh and both carry the heart root — plural construct here, singular in the preceding verse — but the divine name is too dense through the collection (3 of chapter 21's verses, 70 of 915 book-wide) to serve as a driver, and the two heart terms sit in different syntactic slots with no shared clause template, so the contrast between self-assessment and Yahweh's assessment of hearts stands alone and the pairing reads as thematic wisdom-lit texture rather than a deliberate catchword.

rationale: הֵעֵ֬ז (oshb:Prov.21.29) The line opens with a verb for hardening his face, describing the wicked man, and the antithetic close crediting the upright with establishing his own way completes the contrast within the verse; two ketiv/qere notes (pmarks, single witness) fall on the verb and the suffixed noun for way of that closing clause.
rejected_alternative: Reading this together with the no-wisdom-against-Yahweh saying that follows was set aside, since the hardened-face contrast shares no wording with the triple denial of wisdom, understanding, and counsel.
